author: bounded_idea_supply
chronology: Root proposed the stronger positional condition after reporting the first GDT1238 run-envelope result inconclusive. This is not a blinded or preregistered outcome. No GDT1238 output, source text or native data was opened for this review.
proposal_origin: Root; independent algebraic review by bounded_idea_supply.
contract: One source character produces one working glyph, preserving the complete word length and group boundary.
The row for position i>0 is determined only by the immediately previous written output glyph y[i-1]. Each row is a fixed injective mapping, so its inverse on emitted symbols is unique.
The first position may use a public reset row or an arbitrary entry row. No additional position-dependent state, deletion, expansion or within-word reset is allowed.
theorem: For an output run y[a:a+k]=g repeated k times, with zero-based indices and half-open slices, the source substring x[a+1:a+k] is constant and has length k-1.
proof: For every i=a+1,...,a+k-1, both y[i-1] and y[i] equal g.
Thus x[i]=inverse(f_g)(g), the same source symbol at every such position.
The input producing y[a] can differ because its row is determined by the preceding output or entry row. It is not included in the forced constant substring.
necessary_source_envelope: For each observed output run in a complete target word, some candidate source word must have the same whole-word length and a constant substring at exactly the forced positions a+1 through a+k-1 in the chosen processing orientation.

Allowing a different candidate source word for each target run is a generous relaxation. Every genuine writer satisfies this per-run condition, but separate witnesses need not combine into one source word or one common row table.
A source substring longer than the forced k-1 positions is allowed. No maximality or unequal adjacent source symbols are required.
For k=1 the condition is empty; for k=2 it requires only a single source character and therefore adds no repeated-letter condition.
orientation_and_scope: If the contract processes each entire source word in reverse order, inspect these offsets in that reversed source word. Reverse declared units, not ASCII characters inside multi-character working-glyph labels.
Reversing the source processing order is not automatically equivalent to reversing a ciphertext generated by the original left-to-right machine.
The per-run envelope does not establish a common table, global word alignment, source-token multiplicities, frequencies, meanings, or simultaneous compatibility of several runs in one target word.
A negative result excludes only the declared source inventory/population and whole-word/group carrier contract. A positive result means not excluded by this necessary condition.
No native data access, source count, implementation, root-file change or modification of the earlier frozen run-bound proof was performed.
